items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: Kenny Devine gave them to me. They're both very good clarinets.

ctx.x: That's what he said now. I've never been to Europe. And that's what he told me. And he told me he played the albert clarinet. And he said he liked the albert because you've got a broader tone. I said, well, I thought it was my imagination. Because I have heard BAME clarinet players who've got a pretty broad tone too. You know, like Kenny Devine gets a nice fat tone out of the BAME. So does Benny Goodman. Yeah, I've heard fat tones. Benny Goodman gets a fat tone out of the BAME.
Yeah, but still I've heard Benny Goodman when you don't have a microphone sometime and it doesn't come through like when he's up close to the mic. Is that right?
